clue.text: Winning group got round in one!

indicators.note: the group's word surrounds the other letters, as if it had got round them

parts.note: a gang is a group of people
taken as written
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: A team brags that it won by taking a hole in one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'group' looks like part of the definition 'Winning group', but 'Winning' alone defines; 'got round' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Winning and gaining are synonyms when used of acquiring something, as in winning or gaining ground.

clue.text: Too much weight? What would he expect?

definitions.text: Too much weight? What would he expect?

parts.note: a glut is an excess, too much of something
a ton is a unit of weight

explanation.surface: Someone who overeats is bound to put on heavy pounds.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: a heavy eater who would expect excess bulk.
explanation.definitionFit: A greedy eater who overindulges would expect to gain a great deal of bulk.

clue.text: He considers himself in entering dog's name in a race

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the dog's name goes inside the race letters, entering them

parts.note: TT is the Tourist Trophy motorcycle race on the Isle of Man
Rover is a traditional name for a dog

explanation.surface: An owner thinks about entering his dog in a race.
explanation.walkthrough: TT is the Tourist Trophy motorcycle race on the Isle of Man. The second 'in' is only a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone inward-looking is focused on his own thoughts and feelings rather than other people.

clue.text: The same knight rises for a Welsh giant

parts.note: id. is short for idem, Latin for the same

indicators.note: in a down clue, rises means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: Sir is the title of a knight

explanation.surface: An identical knight stands up to a giant from Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rises' reverses SIR to RIS in this down entry. Idris is the legendary giant of Cader Idris, a mountain in Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Idris Gawr is the giant of Welsh legend, said to sit on the summit of Cader Idris.

clue.text: Jersey's cattle ? Yes and no

parts.note: the islands of Jersey and its neighbour each give a name to a breed of cow and a knitted sweater: the same kind of garment as a jersey, but not cattle from Jersey

explanation.surface: Are these cows from the island of Jersey? Partly.
explanation.walkthrough: A jersey and the neighbouring island's knitted fisherman's sweater are much the same garment; the cattle breeds differ.
explanation.definitionFit: Thick knitted woollen sweaters, and a breed of dairy cow, both named after a Channel Island.

clue.text: Father mending roads — earthwork

parts.note: pa is a familiar word for father

indicators.note: mending means the letters of the next word are put back together in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Dad is out repairing the roads while an earthwork is noted.
explanation.walkthrough: A parados is a military term; 'Father' supplies the familiar short form, not a priest.
explanation.definitionFit: A parados is the bank of earth built behind a trench to protect against fire from the rear, a military earthwork.

clue.text: Sports benefits include money

indicators.note: include means the word for benefits takes in the letter for money

parts.note: if something pays, it benefits you
L stands for pounds, as in the sign for sterling

explanation.surface: Athletics brings rewards, including cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'include' puts L inside PAYS. L is the old abbreviation for the pound sterling.
explanation.definitionFit: To sport and to frolic both mean to amuse oneself by taking part in games.

clue.text: Gunmen in new fashioned Ascot wear

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery, the gunners of the British Army
taken as written

indicators.note: new fashioned means the letters of the race meeting's name are fashioned anew into another order

explanation.surface: Soldiers go to Royal Ascot in the latest fashions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new fashioned' rearranges ASCOT to COATS. Ascot is a fashionable English racecourse.
explanation.definitionFit: Waterproof outer coats are something people wear in wet weather.

clue.text: Record nobody made, as reported by the Grossmiths

definitions.text: Record nobody made, as reported by the Grossmiths

parts.words: Record nobody made, as reported by the Grossmiths
parts.note: George and Weedon Grossmith wrote the comic novel of a clerk's daily journal, 'The ... of a Nobody'

explanation.surface: A record that no one made, according to two Victorian humorists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nobody' looks like 'no one', but it refers to Mr Pooter, the Nobody of the Grossmiths' 1892 comic novel.
explanation.definitionFit: A daily record of events is a journal, as kept by the Grossmiths' clerk Charles Pooter.

clue.text: Sitting around Watts showed signs of heat

indicators.note: around means the sitting word wraps itself round the electrical letter

parts.note: seated means sitting down
W is the symbol for watts, units of power

explanation.surface: Those seated near an electric heater began to perspire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts W inside SEATED: S-W-EATED.
explanation.definitionFit: Perspiring is the body's sign of being hot.

clue.text: Issue is complete

definitions.meaning: to issue a sound or remark is to say it out
as an adjective, total or absolute, as in an out-and-out fool

explanation.definitionFit: The verb sense is to give forth speech; the adjective sense is total, as in sheer nonsense.

clue.text: Uproot a tree — acid damage

indicators.note: damage here means the letters of the preceding words are wrecked and rearranged

explanation.surface: Acid rain has harmed a tree so badly it must be pulled up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damage' rearranges A, TREE and ACID together.
explanation.definitionFit: To uproot something is to pull it out by the roots, to wipe it out entirely.

clue.text: Saul slew his, said the women of Israel

definitions.text: Saul slew his, said the women of Israel

parts.words: Saul slew his, said the women of Israel
parts.note: refers to the song in 1 Samuel 18 where the women sang that Saul had slain his many, David his ten times as many

explanation.surface: A Biblical recollection of the victory song for King Saul.
explanation.walkthrough: In 1 Samuel the women sang 'Saul hath slain his thousands, and David his ten thousands'.
explanation.definitionFit: The number Saul's victims reached in the song was a large count in the many hundreds over.

clue.text: Public demand a pint from the vault

parts.note: a public cry is an outcry, a demand voiced by the people
PT is the standard abbreviation for pint

explanation.surface: People call for a pint to be fetched from the cellar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' is a link word; 'the vault' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An underground chamber beneath a church, used for burials, is a vault.

clue.text: Backing understood to cover many requirements

indicators.note: the reversed word wraps around the other letter, covering it
backing means the word for understood is read from its back end to its front

parts.note: something understood has been seen, as in 'I see'
D is the Roman numeral for 500, crosswordese for many

explanation.surface: Supporters understand that many things are required.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backing' turns SEEN into NEES; 'to cover' puts D inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Requirements are things that are wanted or necessary, the plural noun of what one must have.

clue.text: Beryl, perhaps — converse of a bird

parts.note: beryl is a gemstone, a kind of stone
to converse is to chat

explanation.surface: A woman called Beryl talks with a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beryl' looks like a woman's name but is the gem.
explanation.definitionFit: A stonechat is a small European songbird with a call like stones knocked together.

clue.text: Delighted — sing a note in consequence

indicators.note: the singing and note go inside the word for consequence

parts.note: an end is a result or consequence
to chant is to sing
E is one of the musical notes

explanation.surface: Someone thrilled bursts into song as a result.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sing a note' reads as one action, but it splits into a verb for singing and the single letter for a note.
explanation.definitionFit: To be delighted is to be charmed, as though bewitched by a spell.

clue.text: She was unbelievably prophetic

parts.note: 'unbelievably' means not believed rather than amazingly: the Trojan princess cursed by Apollo always foretold the truth but was never believed

explanation.surface: A woman with an uncanny gift for prediction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unbelievably' seems to mean 'astonishingly', but it means she was never believed.
explanation.definitionFit: The Trojan seer whose true prophecies went unheeded, cursed by Apollo.

clue.text: Freshwater shellbacks with land legs

parts.note: terra is Latin for earth or land
pins is informal for legs

explanation.surface: Old sailors who have found their land legs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shellbacks' looks like seasoned sailors, but here it means turtles' shelled backs.
explanation.definitionFit: Freshwater turtles with hard shells, found in North American ponds and rivers.

clue.text: Head backs scholastic groups in pubs

indicators.note: backs here means the word for head turns round and runs backwards

parts.note: the top is the head of something
British schools divide pupils into competing groups called houses

explanation.surface: A headmaster supports school houses meeting in the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: British schools split pupils into houses that compete at sport; 'Head' looks like a headmaster but is just the word for the top.
explanation.definitionFit: A pothouse is an old word for a small, humble tavern, a drinking place.

clue.text: Shady ladies' convenience

parts.note: 'shady ladies' suggests disreputable women, but it is a shade that makes ladies shady, a handy portable sunshade

explanation.surface: A toilet facility for women of doubtful reputation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'convenience' hints at a public toilet in British usage, but it is a handy item giving ladies shade.
explanation.definitionFit: A light umbrella carried to keep off the sun.

clue.text: Lure of sex and drink in the old city

parts.note: SA stands for sex appeal, the lure of sex
rum is a spirit, a drink

explanation.surface: Temptations of the flesh and liquor in an ancient town.
explanation.walkthrough: Old Sarum is the abandoned hilltop site of the original Salisbury in Wiltshire, England; Sarum is also the old name for Salisbury.
explanation.definitionFit: Old Sarum is the ancient settlement that preceded Salisbury, and Sarum is its historic name.

clue.text: " Mastiff, greyhound. -, grim " (Lear)

parts.note: fill the blank in Edgar's list of dogs in King Lear, Act 3 Scene 6: a dog of mixed breed

explanation.surface: A line of Shakespeare naming dogs, with one gap.
explanation.walkthrough: The line in King Lear reads 'Mastiff, greyhound, mongrel grim', from Edgar's list of dogs.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog of mixed or uncertain breeding, completing Shakespeare's list of hounds.

clue.text: Trimming a shrub outside the church

indicators.note: outside means the shrub's letters go round the church's

parts.note: rue is an aromatic evergreen herb or shrub
CH is the usual abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: Someone is pruning a bush that grows beside the church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trimming' suggests pruning the shrub, but it means a dressmaker's frill.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruche is a frill or pleated strip of fabric used as dress trimming.

clue.text: Patch the cuff

definitions.meaning: an archaic word for a patch or piece of cloth for mending
to cuff is to strike with the hand, a blow

explanation.definitionFit: The noun once meant a rag or mending patch; as a verb it means to hit or smack.

clue.text: Seaman who has rows with his girl ?

definitions.text: Seaman who has rows with his girl ?

parts.words: Seaman who has rows with his girl ?
parts.note: reads as a boat plus a swain: a young lover who rows his sweetheart about in a small craft, rather than quarrelling

explanation.surface: A sailor who is always arguing with his girlfriend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rows' suggests quarrels, but it is rowing a boat; a swain is an old word for a young male lover.
explanation.definitionFit: A bosun is the ship's officer in charge of rigging and deck crew, a seaman.

clue.text: Island pub ran out of negro-head

parts.note: a bar is a pub

indicators.note: out of means the following letter is taken out of the word ran

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: head here means only the leading letter of the word before it is wanted

explanation.surface: An islander's pub has run short of tobacco.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' removes N from RAN to leave RA. Negro-head was a dark plug tobacco; Barra is an island in Scotland's Outer Hebrides.
explanation.definitionFit: Barra is one of the islands of the Outer Hebrides off western Scotland.

clue.text: Female shah?

parts.note: the old English title for the Persian ruler is also a girl's name, a form of Sophia

explanation.surface: A woman who rules Persia.
explanation.walkthrough: Sophy was the old English title for the shah of Persia, from the Safavid dynasty, and is also a girl's name.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic title of the Persian monarch that doubles as a feminine name.

clue.text: Desdemona, such a mate, playing chess

definitions.meaning: Othello's wife, killed by a pillow pressed over her face
a checkmate given by a knight to a king hemmed in by its own pieces

explanation.walkthrough: 'mate' looks like spouse, which suits Desdemona, but it is checkmate.
explanation.definitionFit: Desdemona dies suffocated under a pillow, and the knight's mate of a boxed-in king carries the same descriptive name.

clue.text: Poet — one of those who saw the Jackdaw

definitions.meaning: Matthew ... was an English poet of the early 18th century

definitions.text: one of those who saw the Jackdaw
definitions.meaning: in 'The Jackdaw of Rheims' from the Ingoldsby Legends, a monastery head is among the churchmen who see the thieving bird

explanation.definitionFit: Matthew Prior was a poet, and a monastic superior is among the onlookers in the Ingoldsby verse.

clue.text: Taut — lie twisting in old Paris

indicators.note: twisting means the letters of the two words are wrung into a new order

explanation.surface: A tense lie is spun in ancient Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twisting' rearranges TAUT and LIE together.
explanation.definitionFit: Lutetia was the Roman name for the settlement that became Paris.

clue.text: Plutonic article by backward girl

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
taken as written

indicators.note: backward means the word for girl is written back to front

parts.note: a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: A grammar note about a shy girl stands beside a reference to Pluto.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backward' reverses LASS to SSAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Plutonic and abyssal both describe the deep regions, rocks formed far below the surface or the ocean depths.
